claim: [L120-L127] (MED/parser/greedy-match) The greedy wildcard after a parameter's initial value consumes the comment, unit, and description, so those named metadata groups resolve empty even for populated declarations.
other_wording: [L120-L129] (HIGH/parser/metadata-loss) The greedy `.*` after the optional value is followed only by optional metadata groups, so it can consume the entire remainder of every parameter declaration and prevent unit, description, and JSON metadata from being captured.

claim: [L239-L251] (MED/generation/atomicity) Each destination is opened with truncating mode before template rendering, so a render exception can destroy the last valid generated include and leave a partial file.
other_wording: [L239-L251] (MED/generation/validation) Template rendering writes directly to the final `.inc` file with no temporary-file or atomic-replace step, so a render exception can leave a truncated generated source file.

claim: [L149-L166,L175-L192] (MED/schema/validation) Parsed declarations are accepted without checking required JSON keys, name uniqueness, or agreement between declaration rank and JSON shape rank, allowing inconsistent definition data to fail later or generate contradictory Fortran.
[L164-L166,L190-L192] (MED/schema/integrity) Unrestricted dictionary update lets arbitrary JSON metadata overwrite parsed structural fields such as name, type, dimension, or rank.
[L432-L435] (MED/data-loss/string-capacity) The file explicitly acknowledges that the projection string capacity is too short for WKT, so valid projection metadata can be truncated.
other_wording: [L432-L435] (MED/data-truncation) The file explicitly acknowledges that `slen` is too short for WKT yet still stores the projection string in `character(slen)`, so valid projection metadata can be truncated.

claim: [L9-L18] (MED/schema/validation) Parameter classification silently ignores every type other than the three hard-coded spellings and provides no error for an unsupported or misspelled type.
other_wording: [L9-L18] (LOW/generation/type-coverage) Only `double`, `int`, and `char` mapped types enter introspection, with no explicit rejection or handling contract for the other types supported by `generate.py`.

claim: [L11-L18] (MED/schema/maintainability) Array-valued parameters are excluded through manually maintained name lists instead of a rank/shape property, so adding or renaming an array can silently omit it or generate an invalid scalar assignment.
other_wording: [L9-L18,L38,L45,L52] (MED/generation/array-filter) Non-scalar parameters are excluded through a hard-coded name list rather than the available rank metadata, so adding or renaming any array parameter can generate an invalid array-to-scalar assignment.

claim: [L17-L21] (MED/allocation/lifecycle) Indexed allocation is unconditional and has no ASSOCIATED guard or STAT handling, so allocating an already associated component can fail at runtime without a recoverable status.
other_wording: [L17-L21] (MED/allocation/precondition) Generated cases allocate the target pointer without checking whether it is already associated or exposing a failure status, so the caller must satisfy an unstated one-shot precondition.

claim: [L12-L16] (MED/allocation/lifecycle) The indexed deallocator performs an unconditional DEALLOCATE with no ASSOCIATED check or STAT result, so a repeated call or an index whose component was never allocated can raise a Fortran runtime error.
other_wording: [L12-L17] (MED/deallocation/precondition) Generated cases deallocate pointers without an `associated` guard or status result, so repeated or invalid deallocation can raise a runtime error.

claim: [L17-L22] (MED/allocation/error-handling) Reallocation destroys the existing target before attempting an unchecked allocation, so allocation failure loses the prior data and is not surfaced through STAT.
other_wording: [L17-L22] (MED/allocation/data-loss) Reallocation deallocates the old target before allocating the new one, discarding all prior values and leaving no recovery path if allocation fails.

claim: [L17-L21,L33,L38] (LOW/schema/extensibility) The type-to-code mapping is a closed three-entry dictionary with direct lookup, so any definition using an otherwise valid new type causes generation to fail with no validation-oriented diagnostic.
other_wording: [L17-L21,L33,L38] (MED/generation/type-map) The type map expects the key `character`, while `generate.py` maps Fortran character declarations to `char`, and it also omits other generator-supported mapped types, so a newly supported variable type can fail generation with a key error.

claim: [L39-L43] (MED/code-generation/escaping) Definition strings are interpolated directly inside single-quoted Fortran literals without escaping embedded apostrophes, making a legitimate metadata value capable of producing malformed generated source.

[L5-L9] (MED/allocation/lifecycle) Every scalar component is allocated unconditionally without an allocated/associated guard or STAT handling, so a repeated allocation call can terminate at runtime unless an unstated fresh-object precondition always holds.
other_wording: [L5-L9] (MED/allocation/precondition) Scalar allocation is unconditional and has neither an association guard nor allocation-status handling.

claim: [L7-L14] (MED/control-flow/collective-contract) When toall is true the template selects xomaster as the source via iamsrc and xmpi_imaster, but then unconditionally returns on xomaster before any generated distribution body can use that selected source.
other_wording: [L7-L14] (HIGH/mpi/collective-participation) When `toall` is true the code selects the outer communicator and its computational-master root, then immediately returns the outer/output master, leaving a communicator member absent from the following collective distribution and using a nonzero root in helpers that require root zero.
